newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Auto reaches crossroads with new car.
newsitem.headline: Saab Auto reaches crossroads with new car.

text.p: Swedish luxury car maker Saab Auto is banking on its new model, the Saab 9-5, to reverse the company's losses and analysts say success after its launch this June is critical to its future direction.

After posting a loss of 1.24 billion crowns ($167.4 million) in 1996 against flat results a year earlier, Saab Auto has reached a crossroads with just two car models -- the 900 and the 9000 -- on the market.
With owners Swedish investment group Investor AB and General Motors (GM) locked in until 1999, Saab Auto has two years to get back on track before its ownership comes up for review.
GM has expressed commitment to Saab, but Investor has not.

"It is obviously a delicate situation to be so dependent on just two auto models," analyst Gustaf von Essen from brokerage house Carnegie told Reuters. "The 9-5 this summer really has to be a major success."
Saab Auto, owned jointly since 1989, has taken the backseat to competitors in the auto sector in recent years.

"That is the problem with a small manufacturer very dependent on the product cycle. Saab has been a bit slow in replacing its models when other manufacturers have been quick," analyst John Lawson of Salomon Brothers said.
Last week's release of the first pictures of Saab Auto's 9-5 model, which goes on sale from September, was seen as a critical step for Saab Auto, which celebrates 50 years this year.
"I am confident we'll come through and that we, by the year 2000, will be a significant brand in the global premium car market," Saab Auto's president Robert Hendry said.
Hendry said Saab Auto was expected to return to the black during 1998 and by 2000 should be showing an acceptable return with output raised to 150,000 cars a year from 100,000.
Analysts were more hesitant.
"I can't think of one time since 1992 when the company hasn't said its target is 150,000 cars a year," Lawson said.
"But I think Saab Auto now with the research and development strength of General Motors Europe behind it does have a far better chance than it had in the past."
Von Essen said this target would have to be lifted to at least 200,000 by the year 2000, but added Saab Auto needed to succeed with two models before proceeding with a third car line.
"It is a moving target and this is the difficulty in trying to catch up," Von Essen said.
He said Saab had to improve marketing and distribution.

"There's an agreement with GM's Saturn mark in the U.S. and in Sweden with Opel, but to really hit Europe some kind of distribution loop with another General Motors mark is needed, but without mixing the brands."
Saab Auto, managed by GM, has striven to create an image as an exclusive, luxury car, rivalling BMW and Mercedes.
There is some concern that too close a co-operation with GM would destroy this image and the new 9-5, with its new generation of Saab Ecopower engines, might meld into the Opel series.
"From an industrial perspective this is a car that owes quite a lot to the Opel Vectra platform," Lawson said.
"There is a considerable amount of shared component content with the Vectra. It'll be interesting to see how clever the engineers are at making this engine set into two clear models."
Under an agreement in mid-1996, Investor and GM were each to invest 1.74 billion crowns in Saab Auto in 1996-97 in a bid to boost sales by 50 percent over five years.
The agreement also gave GM the right to buy all or part of Investor's 50 percent stake between July 1999 and January 2000.
If the option is not exercised, Investor has the right to sell up to half of its holding to GM by July 2000.
"No-one will make a decision before 1999," Investor's Nils Ingvar Lundin told Reuters. "We could stay on as owners."
GM has a strong commitment to Saab Auto, a spokesman said.
"We have always viewed our Saab investment as a long-term investment," the GM Europe spokesman told Reuters.
"Saab's brand equity is a very positive factor in the marketplace as a premium brand." ($ = 7.407 Swedish Crowns)
